disease_label_per_paper: Acute hemolytic transfusion reactions due to multiple alloantibodies including anti-E, anti-c and anti-Jkb
presentation_summary: 34-year-old man received five packed RBC units during total hip replacement, then required further transfusion nine days later for unexplained hemoglobin drop.
During transfusion of the first two units he developed fever and brown-colored urine; transfusion was stopped.
The next day a further RBC transfusion caused even more severe symptoms during the first unit, leading to transfer.
At admission BP was 110/70, pulse 80/min, temperature 36 C, respiratory rate 20/min, with icteric sclera.
Labs included WBC 6.4 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 8.8 g/dL, platelets 22 x10^9/L, total bilirubin 2.46 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 1.16 mg/dL, LDH 1251 U/L, creatinine 1.2 mg/dL, and haptoglobin below 10 mg/dL.
Antibody identification later detected anti-E, anti-c, and anti-Jkb; this final serology is confirmatory/non-ranking.
